issue.title: TUI app import loads 3292 modules against the 3290 cap (test_app_import_budget)
issue.description:
# CI failure: TUI app import loads 3292 modules against the 3290 cap

## CI failure

- **Node:** `tests/ace/tui/test_app_import_budget.py::test_tui_app_import_stays_under_startup_budget`

Deterministic module-count overrun, not the timing flake. The assertion is `assert 3292 < 3290`:
importing the TUI app loads 3292 modules against the 3290 cap. Reproduced 2026-09-20 in workspace
sase_32 at master `244442ee8` in the full lane, in isolation (twice), and with the working tree's
`src/` changes reverted to `HEAD`.

Distinct from sase-136 (closed 2026-09-19): that fixed wall-clock flakiness by measuring CPU time
and explicitly says "do not raise the CPU budget or module cap". This is the cap itself being
exceeded by two modules, so recent import-graph growth is the suspect; which commit added them is
NOT established. Caveat to rule out first: this workspace's venv also has the required plugins
installed (`setup_required_plugins`), so confirm the count is not plugin-dependent before
bisecting. Fix by removing the new eager imports, not by raising the cap.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic module-count overrun (assert 3292 < 3290), not a timing flake: fails in the full lane, twice in isolation, and with the working tree's src reverted to HEAD. sase-136 already made the timing CPU-based.

payload.description: sase-136 fixed the wall-clock flake in this same test and kept the 3290-module cap; this is that cap now being exceeded by 2 modules, a different root cause
